entries.title: Open question: fixed-length honeycomb SAW from the origin to SLE(8/3)
entries.statement: OPEN QUESTION (not a theorem): Choose uniformly among all n-step self-avoiding walks on the hexagonal lattice starting at the origin. Grimmett's Question 2.2 asks whether, after suitable spatial rescaling as n tends to infinity, the random path converges weakly to an SLE(8/3) curve. The source does not specify the scale exponent, curve topology, or SLE domain/variant; a proposed proof must make these choices explicit.
assumptions: uniform distribution over all such walks

source.excerpt: uniformly distributed n-step SAW from the origin

entries.title: Conjecture: critical chordal honeycomb SAW to SLE(8/3)
entries.statement: CONJECTURE (not proved): In a simply connected proper planar domain with distinct boundary marks a,b, approximate the domain by mesh-delta honeycomb domains. Assign each self-avoiding path between lattice marks near a,b probability proportional to x_c raised to its number of visited vertices, where x_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2)). As delta tends to zero, the path law is conjectured to converge to chordal SLE(8/3) from a to b. The path length varies and both endpoints are prescribed; this is a different ensemble from the uniform fixed-n origin question.

source.excerpt: For x=x_c, the law of gamma_delta ... converges

entries.title: Missing transfer from chordal Boltzmann SAW to fixed-length origin SAW
entries.statement: A scaling limit for critical length-weighted honeycomb self-avoiding paths between prescribed domain boundary points does not by itself establish a scaling limit for uniformly sampled n-step honeycomb self-avoiding walks from the origin. The former randomizes length and fixes both endpoints; the latter fixes length and leaves the endpoint random. An application to the fixed-length question needs an additional theorem controlling the length disintegration, endpoint law, spatial rescaling, and curve topology. No such theorem is supplied by the cited conjectures or this draft.
assumptions: the two sampling rules are as stated in the cited primary questions

source.excerpt: That is a related ensemble, with no transfer theorem supplied here.

entries.title: Cycle kernel of the honeycomb parafermionic vertex relation
entries.statement: Let G be a finite connected subgraph of the honeycomb lattice with vertex set V and internal edge set E, and set all boundary half-edge values to zero. For each internal edge e=uv with midpoint m_e, consider complex midpoint values F satisfying at every v the relation sum_{e incident to v}(m_e-v)F(m_e)=0. The complex solution space has dimension |E|-|V|+1. An interior regular hexagonal face of side delta supports a solution with sup norm one, zero boundary values, and neighboring face-midpoint values differing by one over Euclidean distance sqrt(3)delta/2. Consequently this local equation with bounded values and fixed boundary data alone implies neither uniqueness nor mesh-uniform equicontinuity. These kernel solutions are not asserted to be SAW path-sum observables.
entries.proof_text: Orient each internal edge e from u to v, let d_e=v-u, and set X_e=(d_e/2)F(m_e). The two endpoint contributions are +X_e and -X_e, so the vertex equations are B X=0 for the oriented incidence matrix. Connectedness gives rank(B)=|V|-1 by a spanning tree, hence the dimension formula. On an interior face orient the six edges cyclically and set X_e=delta/2 there and zero elsewhere. Then F(m_e)=delta/d_e on that face, of modulus one. Successive d_e rotate by pi/3, so adjacent F values differ by one; the midpoint spacing is sqrt(3)delta/2.
assumptions: regular interior hexagonal face for the explicit mode
entries.domain: probability; discrete complex analysis; graph linear algebra

entries.title: Local parafermionic vertex relation alone does not give observable compactness
entries.statement: The critical honeycomb self-avoiding-walk parafermionic observable satisfies a local complex vertex relation, but that relation with boundedness and fixed boundary data alone has bounded cycle modes with arbitrarily sharp mesh-scale variation. Therefore any proof of observable convergence must add a condition that controls the actual path-sum observable beyond the local relation. This obstruction does not refute the SAW-to-SLE(8/3) conjecture.
assumptions: no extra path-sum estimate is assumed

source.excerpt: This verifies a bounded non-equicontinuous kernel mode.

relations.rationale: The gap concerns the fixed-length uniform origin ensemble exactly described in Grimmett Question 2.2.
The compared chordal ensemble has prescribed endpoints and critical length fugacity, as stated in Duminil-Copin--Smirnov Conjecture 1.
The explicit bounded face circulation is a counterexample to uniqueness and mesh-uniform equicontinuity from the vertex relation and boundary values alone.
